findings.description: EPOCH OFFSET MISSING — the formula emits a raw Sheets serial, not a count of days since 1970-01-01. SPEC: "...encodes GOOGLEFINANCE's trade date as a locale-proof integer count of days since 1970-01-01 (a TEXT-formatted serial-date DIFFERENCE...)". CODE ({scratch}/audit-H-MARK-008/crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:270-274): `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("{ticker}","tradetime")),"0"),"")` — there is no subtraction of any kind, so the 'difference' the spec names is never computed. Sheets' serial origin is 1899-12-30, so the cell carries serial days, offset +25569 from the spec's stated Unix-epoch encoding. Both directions surface it: all three A runs independently derived the missing term and wrote the SAME constant (A1 `UNIX_EPOCH_SERIAL: i64 = 25_569`, A2 `EPOCH_SERIAL: i64 = 25569`, A3 `UNIX_EPOCH_SERIAL: i32 = 25569`), each tracing it verbatim to 'days since 1970-01-01'; and no B run reconstructed any epoch offset at all — B1/B2/B3 all describe the encoding as merely 'truncated to its whole-day date serial by INT', which is exactly where the code sits and exactly what the spec does not say. This is a live correctness defect, not a wording gap: the consumed type `pt_core::Date` is Unix-epoch days throughout the workspace (crates/sheets-view/tests/marks.rs uses `Date(19_150)`, runtime/tests/reports.rs `Date(19_180)`, formula.rs `Date(19_200)` for a 2022 context). FAILURE: a trade dated 2026-08-01 has Sheets serial 46235; the read-back at crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs:316-323 parses 46235 and stamps `Mark.quote_date = Date(46235)` ≈ 2096-08-19 — every quote-epoch stamp lands ~70 years in the future, poisoning freshness/staleness display (tui theme `Qualifier::Stale { quote_epoch }`) and History `TradingDayKey` keying.

EMPTY / UNPARSEABLE QUOTE DATE SILENTLY BECOMES Date(0) (1970-01-01) INSTEAD OF NO STAMP. SPEC states the cell is 'empty while loading/errored' but is silent on what the settle pass does with an empty stamp — a sub-decision it leaves open. All three A runs independently invented the opposite of the code and flagged it as an invention: A1 `Ok(None)`, A2 `None`, A3 `Ok(None)`, each documenting 'no stamp; settle skips the row / leaves the prior mark untouched'; two of the three additionally treat a non-empty non-integer as a hard error (`QuoteDateParseError::Unparseable` / `QuoteDateError::Unparsable`). CODE (crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs:316-319) does `cells.get(QUOTE_DATE_COL).and_then(|s| s.trim().parse::<i32>().ok()).unwrap_or(0)` → `PriceReading::Numeric { quote_date: Date(0) }` — absent cell, empty cell, and garbage cell all collapse to a real-looking 1970-01-01 stamp, the price reading is still accepted, and nothing degrades. All three B runs pinned this as unstated code law (B1 §006, B2 §6, B3 §5: 'default the quote date to Date(0)... the price is not rejected'). FAILURE: `Price` and `Quote Date` are two independent GOOGLEFINANCE calls that settle at different times; a row whose price has resolved but whose tradetime is still `#N/A` yields a numeric price stamped Date(0), and there is no sentinel distinguishing 'no quote date yet' from a genuine 1970-01-01 quote.

GRID POSITION HARD-PINNED AT ZERO-BASED COLUMN 12 IN TWO CRATES — spec says only 'a companion Quote Date column on the Positions tab', naming no index, no ordering, and no adjacency. Code pins it three independent times: `POSITIONS_HEADER`'s 13th entry (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:187), the test's `assert_eq!(qcol, 12, "Quote Date is the read-back's column-12 companion")` (crates/sheets-view/tests/formula.rs:221-224), and — critically — the reader's own `const QUOTE_DATE_COL: usize = 12` (crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs:300), which is a literal, NOT derived from `POSITIONS_HEADER`. Unanimous across all three B runs (all state 'last (13th) typed header column, zero-based index 12'). FAILURE: inserting any Positions column left of Quote Date updates the writer's header and shifts the emitted cell to index 13, while the reader keeps reading index 12 — it reads the neighbouring `Realized P&L` value (e.g. '1500.00'), fails `parse::<i32>()`, and per the finding above silently degrades to Date(0) rather than raising. Writer and reader share no compile-time link.

QUOTE-DATE INTERPRETATION IS GATED ON THE PRICE CELL'S STATE, not on the quote's own loading/errored state. Spec ties emptiness to the quote itself ('empty while loading/errored'). Code (crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs:301-326) evaluates column 4 first: empty / `Loading...` (ASCII-case-insensitive) / `#N/A` → `Transient`; any other `#`-prefixed value or an unparseable f64 → `Permanent`; column 12 is read ONLY inside the `Ok(price_usd)` arm. So `Transient` and `Permanent` readings carry no quote date at all, and a transiently-unknown symbol keeps its PRIOR mark's own quote_date via the carry-forward in read_marks (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:873-879). All three B runs pin this coupling (B1 §007, B2 §9, B3 §4); the spec never states that the two GOOGLEFINANCE cells are read as one gated unit.

READ-BACK PARSE WIDTH AND NORMALIZATION PINNED BUT UNSTATED — the code fixes the stamp domain at base-10 signed 32-bit with whitespace trimming (`s.trim().parse::<i32>()`, crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs:318); negative day counts are accepted, no range check, no overflow signal. The spec states 'integer count of days' with no width, sign domain, or trimming rule. All three B runs pinned `i32` explicitly (B1 §005, B2 §5, B3 §4); all three A runs chose `i64` instead (A1/A3 `parse::<i64>()`, A2 `QuoteEpochDay(i64)`). The width is silently load-bearing under the epoch defect above: a raw Sheets serial also fits comfortably in i32, so the wrong-epoch value parses cleanly rather than surfacing as an error.

THE FORMULA CARRIES THE ALIAS-RESOLVED TICKER, INLINED AS A QUOTED LITERAL — `quote_date_formula(&ticker)` is fed `resolve_ticker(aliases, symbol)`, the SAME resolved ticker as the row's `Price` formula (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:547, 581, 590), and the test asserts symbol `AMZN` aliased to `NASDAQ:AMZN` renders `NASDAQ:AMZN` inside the quote-date formula (crates/sheets-view/tests/formula.rs:255-265). The spec mentions neither alias resolution, nor the coupling to the Price column's ticker, nor literal-vs-cell-reference. All three B runs pin it as a hard requirement; the A runs split on the underlying open question (A1 and A2 built a `$A{row}` cell reference into the symbol column, A3 inlined a literal with `"`-doubling escaping that the real code does not perform).

PINNED FORMULA CONSTANTS THE SPEC NEVER NAMES: the `"tradetime"` GOOGLEFINANCE attribute (spec says only "GOOGLEFINANCE's trade date"), `INT` truncation toward the day boundary, `TEXT(…,"0")` as the exact locale-proof format, and `IFERROR(…,"")` as the single mechanism covering both loading and errored. All three B runs reproduce the formula string character-for-character as requirement text. A converged on `"tradetime"` (all three, each explicitly flagging it as invented — so the attribute name is under-specified rather than drifted) but split on truncation: A1 omitted `INT` entirely and flagged the resulting hazard that `TEXT` rounds, so an intraday fraction ≥ .5 rolls the reported day forward. The code's `INT` resolves that hazard; the spec text does not.

notes:
Classification is BD-DRIFT because the top two findings are the same gap seen from both sides, and there is a substantial B-only surplus tail underneath.

Why the epoch finding is BD rather than A-only: the A runs unanimously WROTE the `-25569` term (spec-traced, not invented — the spec says both "days since 1970-01-01" and "serial-date difference"), and the B runs unanimously RECONSTRUCTED a spec with no offset at all, describing the encoding as a bare "date serial". Neither direction had to guess; they simply landed on opposite sides of the same missing subtraction.

The test suite is structurally blind to it, which is why it survived. crates/sheets-view/tests/formula.rs:237-253 asserts only substring containment — `contains("GOOGLEFINANCE")`, `contains("tradetime")`, `contains("TEXT(")`, `contains("IFERROR")` — and never evaluates or arithmetically checks the emitted formula. The one place writer and reader could compose, crates/runtime/tests/adapters.rs:177-224, hand-writes `row[12] = Cell::Value("19180".to_string())` — a Unix-epoch day count — instead of calling `quote_date_formula`, then asserts it reads back as `Date(19_180)`. That test encodes the SPEC's convention while the production formula emits the other one; the two halves of the contract are never run against each other anywhere in the workspace. Every other quote_date in the suite (marks.rs, cycle.rs, reports.rs, boot.rs, e2e_real_sheets.rs) is a hand-injected `Date(19_1xx)` through the in-memory fake, bypassing `price_reading_from_cells` entirely.

Stability, A: high. All three produced the same formula shape (IFERROR-wrapped, TEXT(…,"0"), tradetime, minus 25569), the same empty→soft-skip read-back semantics, and near-identical assumption lists. Divergences are confined to spec-open sub-decisions: symbol as cell reference (A1, A2) vs. inlined literal (A3); INT truncation (A2, A3) vs. none (A1); an extra `N(...)=0` loading sentinel (A2).

Stability, B: high — the highest agreement of the two. All three reproduce the formula string identically, pin index 12 / 13th column, pin `Cell::Formula` typing, pin alias-resolved ticker shared with Price, pin trimmed-i32 parsing from column 12, and pin the `Date(0)` default with the price still accepted. Differences are organizational (B1 numbers 8 clauses, B3 collapses to 5) rather than substantive.
